text:
Michael Carcone has played 12 of Utah's 21 games, with a long gap between early October and the start of November, and he has one goal and three points. On a team missing Dylan Guenther, Nick Schmaltz and others, his minutes matter more than they usually would.

The goals will come. One goal on 2.2 expected in 12 games is cold, and he's put 27 shots on goal in barely 12 minutes a night, which is the volume of a scorer. Utah takes 56% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on. Last season he scored 16 goals in 79 games, and our talent range has him around 14 for this one.

He's an undrafted 30-year-old who worked his way up through the AHL, and his game has quirks worth watching. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 54% of his entries and making 18% of his setups from behind the net, more than twice a typical forward's rate. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 95th percentile for driving play after adjusting for teammates. That's a useful player on a depleted team. The points should follow the chances.
